title.justification: The paper titled 'Pseudo AI Bias' explores the concept of pseudo AI bias (PAIB) and its implications on society.
title.quote: Pseudo Artificial Intelligence bias (PAIB) is broadly discussed in the literature, which can result in unnecessary AI fear in society, thereby exacerbating the enduring inequities and disparities in accessing and sharing the benefits of AI applications and wasting social capital invested in AI research.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the concept of pseudo AI bias (PAIB), which includes misunderstandings, pseudo-mechanical bias, and over-expectations of AI. It emphasizes the negative impact of PAIB on society, such as exacerbating inequities, generating social fear of AI, and wasting resources invested in AI technology. The study reviews literature to conceptualize PAIB, presents its types, impacts, and proposes solutions to address them to improve AI's societal trust and application.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on identifying and discussing pseudo AI biases rather than directly addressing sustainable development or ecological concerns.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Pseudo Artificial Intelligence bias (PAIB) is broadly discussed in the literature, which can result in unnecessary AI fear in society, thereby exacerbating the enduring inequities and disparities in accessing and sharing the benefits of AI applications and wasting social capital invested in AI research.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecologically-related sustainable development areas. Its main theme revolves around biases in AI technology.
primary_category.quote: The study systematically reviews publications in the literature to present three types of PAIBs identified due to: a) misunderstandings, b) pseudo-mechanical bias, and c) over-expectations.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's themes do not engage with specific climate or ecological sustainability topics.
secondary_categories.quote: To conceptualize and study these “biases,” we coined the term pseudo AI bias (PAIB). Attributing PAIB to AI is unfair and can disadvantage the potential of technologies in education.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories related to climate or ecological topics do not apply to this paper as it explores AI bias.
primary_sub_category.quote: While AI biases may result from deficit design, skewed training data, confounding of the algorithmic models, or the algorithm computational capacity, some are not. Defining AI bias and attributing bias outcomes to AI needs to be cautious.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainability are discussed in the paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This paper investigates pseudo AI bias, focusing on misunderstandings, pseudo-mechanical biases, and overexpectations of algorithmic predictions.

applications.value: Addressing pseudo AI biases to improve societal trust in AI
applications.justification: The study suggests solutions to mitigate AI fears and biases, aiming to improve societal trust and the equitable sharing of AI benefits.
applications.quote: We discussed the consequences of and solutions to PAIBs, including certifying users for AI applications to mitigate AI fears, providing customized user guidance for AI applications, and developing systematic approaches to monitor bias.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no indication that a new category is necessary as the paper does not focus on sustainable development practices.
new_primary_category.quote: Pseudo Artificial Intelligence bias (PAIB) is broadly discussed in the literature, which can result in unnecessary AI fear in society, thereby exacerbating the enduring inequities and disparities in accessing and sharing the benefits of AI applications and wasting social capital invested in AI research.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper is centered on social AI biases, not requiring a new sub-category within the sustainable development spectrum.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We first review the definition of bias to identify the criteria for conceptualizing PAIBs. We then present three types of PAIBs identified in the literature and discuss the potential impacts of PAIBs on education and society.
